title: Writing Your First Chart 📝
description: Create a Helm chart from scratch using `helm create` and understand templates.

slides.title: Scaffolding a Chart 🏗️
slides.content:
# `helm create` gives you a skeleton

```bash
helm create mychart
```

Generates a directory structure:
```
mychart/
├── Chart.yaml          # metadata
├── values.yaml         # default configuration
├── charts/             # sub‑charts
├── templates/          # Kubernetes resource templates
│   ├── deployment.yaml
│   ├── service.yaml
│   ├── hpa.yaml
│   ├── ingress.yaml
│   ├── _helpers.tpl    # reusable template helpers
│   ├── NOTES.txt       # post‑install message
│   └── tests/          # test resources
└── .helmignore
```

slides.title: Chart.yaml – The Metadata Card 📇
slides.content:
```yaml
apiVersion: v2
name: mychart
version: 0.1.0
appVersion: "1.16.0"
description: A Helm chart for Kubernetes
type: application
keywords:
  - web
home: https://example.com
sources:
  - https://github.com/example/repo
maintainers:
  - name: Your Name
    email: you@example.com
```
- `apiVersion: v2` is the Helm 3 format.
- `type` can be `application` or `library` (helper charts).

quizData.question: Which file contains the chart name and version?
quizData.explanation: Chart.yaml holds chart metadata like name, version, and description.

slides.title: Templates and the Go Template Language 📄
slides.content:
# Dynamically generate Kubernetes YAML

Templates use Go’s `text/template` syntax plus Sprig functions. Example from `deployment.yaml`:
```yaml
replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount }}
```

Built‑in objects:
- `.Values` – user values from `values.yaml` and `--set`.
- `.Release` – release name, namespace, revision.
- `.Chart` – contents of `Chart.yaml`.
- `.Files` – access to files in the chart.
- `.Template` – current template info.

You can use conditionals, loops, and functions: `{{ if .Values.service.enabled }}...{{ end }}`, `{{- range .Values.env }}...{{ end }}`.

slides.title: Template Example: Service
values.yaml – User‑Configurable Settings ⚙️
slides.content:
## The default configuration

```yaml
replicaCount: 1
image:
  repository: nginx
  tag: ""
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
service:
  type: ClusterIP
  port: 80
resources: {}
```

Users can override any value with `--set` or `-f`. Keep your values well‑documented (comments) because they are the user interface of your chart.

quizData.question: What does `{{ .Values.replicaCount }}` access?
quizData.explanation: It reads the `replicaCount` key from the chart's values.

slides.title: Packaging and Distributing Charts 📦
slides.content:
## Create a .tgz package

```bash
helm package ./mychart       # creates mychart-0.1.0.tgz
```

To serve a repository, generate an `index.yaml`:
```bash
helm repo index . --url https://my-repo.example.com
```
Then host the directory with any HTTP server.

You can also push to OCI registries (`helm push` with OCI support).

quizData.question: Which command creates a chart archive?
quizData.explanation: `helm package` bundles the chart directory into a .tgz file.
